column3: Close to the Greek.
NASB has “He,” not “Jesus,” like the critical text; “in their midst” is rendered “before them.”
“Turn” is rendered “are converted,” and “little children” is “children.”
“The greater” is rendered “the greatest.”
Close to the Greek.
“Sunk” is rendered “drowned.”
“Causes of sin” is rendered “stumbling blocks,” and “necessary” is “inevitable.”
Close to the Greek.
“The hell of fire” is rendered “the fiery hell.”
“Through all” (always) is rendered “continually.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NASB prints it in braces, following the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the critical text with “leave … and go.”
Close to the Greek.

NASB has “sins” without “against you,” a word the critical text includes in brackets; “reprove him” is “show him his fault.”
“Declaration” is rendered “fact”; the quotation is in capitals.
“Pagan” is rendered “Gentile.”
Close to the Greek; NASB keeps the future perfect “shall have been bound.”
NASB has no “truly,” which the critical text includes.

NASB renders “a man, a king” as “a king” and “servants” (douloi) as “slaves.”
NASB renders “debtor” as “one who owed.”
“The master” is rendered “his lord”; NASB adds “the means.”
NASB follows the critical text with no “Lord”; “bowing on his knees” is “prostrated himself.”
“Master” is rendered “lord,” and “servant” is “slave.”
NASB renders “if you owe anything” as “what you owe.”
NASB follows the critical text without “at his feet” and without “all.”
Close to the Greek.
